upstream_1116_1117.mechanism: ACT's select_action keeps a deque _action_queue of n_action_steps actions and pops one per call; reset() replaces it with an empty deque (or resets the temporal ensembler). At a445d9c nothing between episodes called reset(), so a deque left non-empty at the end of one episode (early exit, or an episode length that is not a multiple of n_action_steps) supplied the first actions of the next episode from old observations. At 6163daa the reset at control_loop entry empties it before any action of the new episode.

readings: one episode per client process: start() calls Ready, which resets the server's observation queue and predicted-timestep set; latest_action is never reset; there is no in-process reset path, so an early reset with queued actions and a late response after a reset are not reachable in this program as written (constructed controls only)

one sequential receiver thread issues one GetActions call at a time and the server predicts from a one-slot observation queue, so chunks arrive in production order; out-of-order arrival and duplicate delivery are not reachable here (constructed controls only)

_aggregate_action_queues builds the future queue only from the incoming chunk: overlapping timesteps are aggregated (default: the arriving action wins) and queued actions whose timesteps the incoming chunk does not cover are dropped; the incoming chunk starts at the observation's timestep, which is the latest performed action, so its horizon always extends beyond the old queue and a wholly obsolete arrival that empties the queue is not reachable under the client's own control loop
a late chunk has its leading actions (timesteps <= latest_action) skipped and its tail admitted; queue starvation while waiting is a useful-execution cost, not an identity violation

timestamps: observations and actions carry the client's time.time(); action timestamps are t_0 + i * environment_dt with t_0 the observation's client timestamp, so the client's logged server_to_client_latency is the client-clock round trip including inference, not a server-to-client one-way latency; the server logs receive_time - obs_timestamp across two hosts' wall clocks without a declared mapping; neither quantity gates control decisions, and no age limit is enforced anywhere

identity: the timestep is an integer control step, the only identity carried by observations and actions; there is no request, chunk, episode or configuration identity on the wire; the server skips an observation whose timestep it already predicted unless must_go is set
